observations:
Torah #83 is a very short, tightly unified teaching (8 lines) built entirely around a single eitza chain. The teaching presents one gematria-based insight — that the six letters of the aleph-beis that contain the sound 'peh' sum (6 × 80) to 480, which is the gematria of Lilith, and that giving charity in secret redeems holy sparks from this klipah by flipping the word אף (anger, gematria 81) into פא (the letter peh, the same two letters reversed) — which the verse expresses as יכפה ('overturns').

The criteria for a new package are: three or more concepts connected by explicit bechina (shared-nature) language forming an independent conceptual domain. This Torah meets none of those criteria:

1. ZERO concepts are connected by bechina language in the source text.
2. The source text uses no form of the phrase 'X הוא בחינת Y', 'X נקרא Y', or any other bechina marker.
3. All relationships in the teaching are strictly causal / transformational: the klipah feeds on the letters and produces impurity; giving tzedakah in secret causes redemption of sparks and letter-transformation.
4. The structural 'clusters' that appear in the text — (a) the klipah-system (Lilith, the six peh-letters, impurity, fire) and (b) the remedy-system (tzedakah in secret, holy sparks, the letter flip) — are connected to each other only by eitza (cause/effect), not by bechina. Within each cluster, the connections are also transformative (the klipah 'becomes' anger from peh; the sparks are 'redeemed'; the letter is 'overturned'), not parallel-nature statements.

Conclusion: Torah #83 is a pure eitza teaching. It contains no bechina structure and no conceptual equivalences that would support package formation. This is itself a meaningful structural observation: some Torahs in Likutay Moharan are pure practical-causal teachings without the bechina scaffolding that characterizes the longer, more encyclopedic Torahs.
